contract.words: Collect $60,000 of settled cash within 30 days using no up-front capital.

terms.proofCondition: $60,000 of settled cash received in the owner's account within 30 days

strategy.title: No plan: the counted PI-agency market cannot carry $60,000
strategy.why: The only opening sells one $150 template pack per agency to a market research counted whole: 310 licensed agencies, one pack each. Even if every agency bought, that is 310 x $150 = $46,500, below the $60,000 target; at the measured 33/300 conversion it is about 34 sales, roughly $5,100.

alternatives.title: Sell the pack to all 310 agencies
alternatives.why: Caps at $46,500 even at 100% conversion; about $5,100 at the measured 11% rate.

steps.label: Search for further openings outside the counted PI-agency market (other buyer populations or a repeat product) that could close the gap

sources.claim: The state licensing board's public licensee search lists 310 licensed PI agencies, each needing one pack.
Comparable investigator case-file template packs sell for $150.

noPlan.decisiveGap: Market volume: the whole counted market (310 agencies x one $150 pack) is worth at most $46,500, below the $60,000 target, so no number of contacts reaches it.
noPlan.resolution: Lower the target to at most $46,500 (realistically about $5,100 at the measured 11% conversion), or find additional openings in uncounted markets; Brain keeps searching for them.

constraints.suggestion: Lower the target to at most $46,500 (310 agencies x $150); about $5,100 is what the measured 33/300 conversion supports in 30 days.

brain.summary: INFEASIBLE AS STATED: the openings held sell into markets research counted whole: every buyer in them agreeing at the top price brings at most $46,500, so they cannot reach the $60,000 still needed. To make it supportable, target: lower the target to about $46,500, the most the openings held bring with every buyer agreeing at the top price. The conclusion covers the openings held; markets nobody has counted are not ruled out, so Brain keeps searching for openings outside them.

card.payer: Licensed private investigators who run their own agencies
card.reachableChannel: Published agency emails in the state licensing board's public licensee search
card.offerScope: One template pack per agency; delivered at once; paid by card at checkout.

links.basis: reach: Published agency emails in the state licensing board's public licensee search
measured on this offer's own sales: 33 accepted of 300 contacts

3 days to usable cash against 30 left

facts.value: The state licensing board's public licensee search lists 310 licensed private-investigator agencies, each with a published email; each needs one pack.
Sell One template pack per agency; delivered at once; paid by card at checkout. to each buyer.
Licensed private investigators who run their own agencies
Comparable investigator case-file template packs sell for $150 on the state investigators' association store (listing prices, 2026-11).

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is right and the decisive gap is a genuine constraint, not missing evidence. Recomputed: the market is counted whole from the state licensing board's licensee search (310 agencies, one pack each, no repeat purchase stated); 310 x $150 = $46,500 < $60,000 even at 100% conversion, so ceil(60000/150) = 400 deals would be needed against 310 buyers (Brain: MARKET_VOLUME false). At the measured 33/300 (11%) conversion the market yields about 34 sales = ~$5,100. Every other link is established (price, conversion on this offer's own sales, Brain-proved spreadsheet fulfilment, $2 cost, $0 exposure, 3-day settlement in a 30-day window), so volume alone decides it. decisiveLinks [MARKET_VOLUME] and the TARGET constraint with basis buyerVolume + price match Brain's own INFEASIBLE AS STATED verdict, and the resolution correctly says the conclusion covers only the counted market and further openings are still searched.
findings: NOTE: The price source text reads 'comparable investigator case-file template packs sell for $150', which on its own is a benchmark of what other sellers charge; it is acceptable here only because the 33/300 acceptances were measured on this offer at its $150 card price. The cap would move only with evidence that these agencies pay more than $194 per pack, of which there is none.

NOTE: 300 of the 310 agencies have already been contacted, so the realistic remaining reach is close to the ~$5,100 the revision states, not $46,500; the 'lower the target to $46,500' suggestion is a ceiling, not an expectation.
